summary: @brick-v2/icons exfiltrates CI/cloud credentials via native addon on require()
details: The package presents a minimal index.js stub exposing empty forRoot/createLogger symbols that resemble an Angular icons module. The only runtime effect of require('@brick-v2/icons') is to load a platform-specific native addon from prebuilds/<platform>-<arch>/metrics.node inside a try/catch that suppresses failures. The ELF binary imports getenv/socket/connect/gethostbyname/fork/setsid and contains strings for credential-grade environment variables (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN, NODE_AUTH_TOKEN, ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN, ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN, SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN) alongside hostname/user/cwd fields. On load it reads those variables and transmits them via a raw socket POST /native HTTP/1.0 request to oob.s4yhii.com, daemonizing via fork/setsid to continue after the host process exits. The JS surface is a decoy; the opaque native binary is the entire payload. Package coordinates (@brick-v2 scope, 'icons' name, version 999.0.1) are consistent with a dependency-confusion lure targeting internal/CI builds.
